shared_assumptions.atomic_transitions: Lease and rate transitions are serialized. A Rust implementation must establish the corresponding lock, actor or atomic-operation discipline.
shared_assumptions.internal_callback_tokens: Completion tokens originate in the internal reservation lifecycle. The model does not expose a completion API to unauthenticated network senders.
shared_assumptions.nonwrapping_generations: Count generations are mathematical naturals. A finite machine identifier needs a no-wrap or generation-collision argument.
shared_assumptions.complete_event_refinement: Every relevant implementation event and error path is represented by the modeled transition.
shared_assumptions.trusted_clock: Only the trusted monotonic clock issues ticks. One modeled tick has a specified real duration and is never replayed or fabricated by peer traffic.
shared_assumptions.cost_dominance: Each supplied weight bounds real per-entry or per-start cost in a common unit, including the allocated state charged to that component.
shared_assumptions.fifo_projection: The waiting rank correctly projects a critical FIFO queue; later critical work is enqueued behind the fixed target request.
shared_assumptions.scheduled_rounds: A completed modeled round really services one critical request. The runtime must execute enough such rounds to establish a wall-clock bound.
shared_assumptions.executor_wakeup: The executor honors the modeled wakeup request and eventually gives a pending poll another turn.
shared_assumptions.authenticated_membership: The verified flag includes full signature checking and authenticated binding of the record to its committee identity and presented epoch.
shared_assumptions.stable_committee_index: Each current committee member has one stable, unique slot. Record senders cannot choose another member slot or create new roster slots.
shared_assumptions.atomic_policy_publication: Each complete policy view is immutable; generation comparison and publication are atomic. Receipt validation and the resulting authorization linearize with publication, or retain equivalent protection through use.
shared_assumptions.policy_input_validation: Health, epoch, membership mappings, roster and the positive recovery threshold come from validated authoritative inputs. Snapshot generation orders local publication, not external governance versions. Input freshness and epoch ordering require separate validation.
shared_assumptions.policy_receipt_provenance: Admission receipts are internal results of policy queries for the actual authenticated peer. Untrusted input cannot construct or alter a receipt, its identity or its allowed flag.
shared_assumptions.stable_resource_configuration: Bucket capacity and pending-pool capacity are fixed during each modeled run. Restarts and runtime resource-cap changes require additional transitions and proofs.
shared_assumptions.canonical_source_keys: Each Count key represents one canonical validated source or prefix under a fixed normalization policy. PeerIds cannot choose or reset this binding. The initial runtime table has unique canonical keys.
shared_assumptions.source_restriction_classification: SourceClear means no unexpired rate debt or ban. The supplied restriction preserves all security-relevant state. Only the modeled registration and eviction events touch the table during a run; trusted expiry, concurrent charging and restart require separate transitions and refinement.

claims.property: A free lease becomes owned, while an already held lease refuses another reservation and keeps its state.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine the real reservation point and ConnectionId ownership.

claims.property: A completion without an owned reservation cannot refund or alter a lease.
open_implementation_obligations: Connect refusal-before-reservation and free-slot callbacks to the no-owner case.

claims.property: Failure, establishment, established-hook refusal, timeout and cancellation each release the matching pending lease.
open_implementation_obligations: Prove coverage of every Rust terminal callback and cancellation path.

claims.property: Repeated terminal callbacks with the same token have no further effect, even when their reason differs.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine duplicate callbacks and their ordering to serialized transitions.

claims.property: After release and reuse, an old token cannot release the new owner; the result extends to arbitrarily later generations.
open_implementation_obligations: Establish the actual ConnectionId/generation mapping and reuse discipline.

claims.property: Every finite sequence of reserve and completion actions preserves the original pool capacity and bounds pending occupancy by it.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine real connection maps, total capacity and all release paths.

claims.property: Available slots plus occupied slots equal the original capacity after any lifecycle trace.
open_implementation_obligations: Connect both implementation counters to the same authoritative ownership map.

claims.property: Distinct queue, pending and established entry costs compose into a weighted retained-resource bound.
open_implementation_obligations: Establish each counter cap, each measured or proved cost bound, and every omitted allocation.

claims.property: Pending retained cost remains bounded throughout arbitrary modeled lifecycle traces on both swarms.
open_implementation_obligations: Link every actual swarm and worker pool, including shared allocations, to the aggregate accounting.

claims.property: Handshake starts over any finite trace cannot exceed initial credit plus issued trusted credit.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine every real handshake-start site and credit debit to the shared state.

claims.property: Refill and attempt transitions preserve the token bucket capacity throughout any trace.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine initial credit, saturating arithmetic and the configured capacity.

claims.property: Eviction and new identities do not reset or replenish the process-wide handshake allowance.
open_implementation_obligations: Prove real source-table eviction, prefix normalization, restart and anti-reset behavior. Per-source penalties are not covered by this global-budget property.

claims.property: Policy invalidation or recovery cannot replenish the global handshake budget.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine actual policy transitions without reinitializing rate state.

claims.property: Peer-claimed clock values cannot issue credit; trusted ticks issue exactly the configured rate per tick.
open_implementation_obligations: Connect modeled ticks to monotonic elapsed time and exclude tick replay, wrap and peer-controlled input.

claims.property: The shared process admits at most burst plus rate times trusted ticks, across arbitrary source and swarm interleavings.
open_implementation_obligations: Use one authoritative balance in all real swarms, choose production burst/rate values and qualify honest reconnect fairness.

claims.property: A per-handshake cost bound lifts the burst-plus-rate envelope to a weighted work bound.
open_implementation_obligations: Establish worst-case cost for actual crypto/parsing paths and separately bound prevalidation work.

claims.property: Bounded polling partitions a finite input into processed events and retained backlog without losing events.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine the real inner transport poll, including Accept, Retry, Refuse and Ignore outcomes.

claims.property: Budget exhaustion with remaining work requests another wakeup, including a Retry-only backlog.
open_implementation_obligations: Connect the modeled flag to a real registered waker and prove the runtime progress premise.

claims.property: A fixed critical request with n predecessors is served after at least n+1 completed service rounds, independently of later bulk arrivals.
open_implementation_obligations: Prove real queue ordering, one critical service per round, and the wall-clock scheduling/hold-time bounds.

claims.property: Bulk arrivals and critical arrivals enqueued behind a waiting request do not increase its waiting rank.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine the actual per-class service queues and admission paths.

claims.property: Unverified records and records from an older epoch do not alter current-committee evidence.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine signature/epoch binding and the actual current-committee lookup.

claims.property: Repeating a record for the same member is idempotent and cannot advance the close decision.
open_implementation_obligations: Prove that all duplicate wire records map to the same verified committee slot.

claims.property: An epoch reset clears old resolution evidence and cannot close with a positive required record count.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine committee transition ordering, roster replacement and the selected recovery threshold.

claims.property: Record updates preserve roster capacity and bound resolution by the number of roster slots.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine the actual roster cardinality, storage and membership-to-slot mapping.

claims.property: A policy action observed at an older view generation cannot replace the current view.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine an atomic comparison and publication operation for every policy callback; preserve the generation actually observed.

claims.property: Whole-view generations advance on replacement, never decrease, and grow by at most the finite policy event count.
open_implementation_obligations: Advance the generation for every effective policy, recovery, membership or health change.
Establish a machine-counter limit or a safe exhaustion protocol; natural-number proofs do not justify wrapping.

claims.property: Admission, peer management and the optional TLS consumer return the same authenticated decision from one captured view.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine each real consumer to the same contract and coherent captured snapshot.
Prove the authentication flag belongs to the queried peer, including TLS stage ordering.

claims.property: An internal admission receipt retains a current decision and cannot be retargeted to another identity or applied after its view or epoch changes.
open_implementation_obligations: Bind receipt identity to the actual authenticated PeerId and preserve unforgeable internal provenance.
Linearize validation and authorization with publication, or retain protection through use; a separate check followed by an unprotected use is insufficient.

claims.property: Missing, stale and contradictory policy faults select Grace while every policy reader still requires authentication.
open_implementation_obligations: Implement correct fault detection and authoritative policy validation; constructors do not establish real freshness.
Retain payload signature and protocol-validity checks beyond this admission predicate.

claims.property: Policy replacement initializes the new roster without resolution evidence, and invalidation clears evidence before a future Closed decision.
open_implementation_obligations: Derive the positive threshold from current committee size minus f and reject invalid configurations.
Establish record timestamp freshness, safe external policy ordering and epoch provenance.

claims.property: Unverified, epoch-mismatched and duplicate policy records cannot create a recovery update; duplicate callbacks do not advance the view generation.
open_implementation_obligations: Verify signature, epoch and committee-identity binding before setting the verified flag.
Refine deduplication and the unique member-to-slot mapping across callbacks and committee changes.

claims.property: A verified current-epoch record for an unresolved roster member has an enabled resolution update.
open_implementation_obligations: Connect actual authenticated records to the modeled updates and derive the closure threshold.
Prove delivery, retry and scheduler fairness separately; this enabled transition is not a wall-clock recovery theorem.

claims.property: An arbitrary finite interleaving of policy, handshake and pending events has exactly the component states of the corresponding projected traces.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine all real events to the joint state, including failures, cancellation and concurrent callbacks.
Extend the transition system for restarts and resource-cap reconfiguration before claiming those paths.

claims.property: A policy change cannot mint shared handshake credits or alter pending ownership.
open_implementation_obligations: Show actual fallback, recovery and policy reload preserve counters and owned reservations.
Account for policy snapshot allocation costs separately from handshake and pending state.

claims.property: Under mixed policy and transport traces, credits stay within capacity and handshake starts do not exceed initial credit plus trusted issuance.
open_implementation_obligations: Wire both swarms and every real handshake start into one aggregate budget.
Relate trusted credit issuance to elapsed time and preserve debt across restart or limit changes.

claims.property: Under mixed policy and transport traces, pending occupancy stays within initial capacity and occupied plus available slots is conserved.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine all ConnectionId ownership and terminal paths to the same pool, including policy transitions.
Establish the configured global cap and preserve per-source attribution and honest reconnect behavior.

claims.property: Source registration and eviction over any finite churn trace preserve the initial slot capacity and keep resident cardinality within it.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine the allocated source map, auxiliary indexes, diagnostics and exporters to one bounded table with a configured slot capacity.
Account for per-entry byte cost and bound retention time. This model proves cardinality, not timed expiry or memory usage.

claims.property: Unvalidated sources cannot register or receive registration permission, a refused registration leaves the table unchanged, and registering a known key leaves its existing table state unchanged.
open_implementation_obligations: Connect reachability to verified QUIC tokens and canonical source/prefix extraction in both swarms.
Prove initial key uniqueness and its preservation in the runtime map, including sources behind shared NAT.
Connect registration to actual per-source rate and pending-occupancy counters; registration permission alone does not authorize a handshake.

claims.property: Any finite registration/eviction churn trace preserves each pre-existing modeled rate-debt or ban record, including its key and slot.
open_implementation_obligations: Refine every eviction and re-registration path, and prove admission actually enforces preserved security state.
Extend the restriction model to simultaneous rate debt and bans, new charges, trusted expiry, policy changes and restart persistence.
Qualify retention, eviction selection, hub population and honest reconnect fairness. The model deliberately allows a fully protected table to refuse new sources.

claims.property: A full table cannot allocate and refuses unknown-source registration; available head slots can register new validated keys, and matching clear entries can be evicted, including in singleton traces.
open_implementation_obligations: Make overflow refusal explicit in the implementation and preserve the independent process-wide handshake budget.
Choose and qualify a bounded retention/expiry policy and honest-source admission behavior under saturation; these safety results do not establish liveness.
